Sanjeev Raghuvanshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12
September, 2024
 Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Gwl:15731
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

On The 12th Of September, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 27215 of 2024
 Sanjeev Raghuvanshi
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Rajmani Bansal and Shri Kapil Singhal - Advocates
 petitioner.
 Shri A.P.S. Tomar- Public Prosecutor for respondent/St
 Shri Girraj Soni- Advocate for respondent No.2.
 Order

By invoking inherent powers of this Court, the present petition has been preferred by petitioner under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.1028 of 2023 registered at Police Station Cantt., District Guna (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 506 of IPC against the petitioner as well as the consequential proceedings on the basis of compromise.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the prosecutrix is a major lady aged around 20 years and she is married.
Prosecutrix happens to be sister-in-law of the petitioner but even then she made relations with the petitioner and later on levelled allegations of rape which are absolutely absurd.

Prima facie, no offence under Section 376 of the IPC is made out NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15731 2 MCRC-27215-2024 against the petitioner.
It has further been submitted that the prosecutrix is a consenting party, as she has made physical relations with her own consent.

3. Apart from the aforesaid facts, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner and the complainant/prosecutrix have entered into a compromise for which they have filed applications i.e. I.A. Nos.12740 & 12741 of 2024 under Sections 320(1), 320(2) of IPC, duly supported by their affidavits.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon the recent judgment rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kapil Gupta Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Another passed in Criminal Appeal No.1217 of 2022 decided on 10.8.2022 in which a criminal case under Section 376 IPC against the petitioner therein was considered for quashment of FIR on the basis of compromise wherein the Sanjeev Raghuvanshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8284372/

sentences.text: Hon'ble Supreme Court while considering the dictum in the case of Narinder Singh Vs. State of Punjab reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466 held in para 13 and 14 that if there is insufficient evidence and by virtue of compromise there is no chance of conviction and the settlement between the parties is going to result into harmony between them which may improve their mutual relationship then at primary stage on such compromise, proceedings may be quashed.

entities.text: Narinder Singh Vs. State of Punjab reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Para 13 and 14 of Kapil Gupta (supra) are material and thus reproduced for ready reference and convenience:

"13. It can thus be seen that this Court has clearly held that though the Court should be slow in quashing the proceedings wherein heinous and serious offences are involved, the High Court is not foreclosed from examining as to whether there exists material for incorporation of such an offence or as to whether there is sufficient evidence which if proved would lead to proving the charge for the offence charged with.

The Court has also to take into consideration as to whether the settlement between the parties NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15731 3 MCRC-27215-2024 is going to result into harmony between them which may improve their mutual relationship.
14. The Court has further held that it is also relevant to consider as to what is stage of the proceedings.

It has been observed that if an application is made at a belated stage wherein the evidence has been led and the matter is at the stage of arguments or judgment, the Court should be slow to exercise the power to quash the proceedings.

However, if such an application is made at an initial stage before commencement of trial, the said factor will weigh with the court in exercising its power."
5.

It is further submitted that in compliance of order passed by this Court, the factum of compromise has been verified by the Principal Registrar of this Court, who has recorded the statements of complainant as well as petitioner - accused and has submitted the report to the effect that the parties have arrived at compromise voluntarily without any threat, inducement and coercion.

6. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the State has opposed the prayer so made by counsel for the petitioner submitting that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in catena of decisions has reiterated the legal position that in heinous and serious offences like murder or rape, the Court should not quash the criminal proceedings, therefore, the present petition filed under Section 482 of CrPC for quashment of FIR and further proceedings deserves to be dismissed.

He referred to a judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Anr. reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303.
7.

sentences.text: even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the Court can be saved and utilised in other material cases.

9. In the case of Ranjeet Kumar Vs. State of H.P. and Ors. (2023 SCC Online HP 1625), the hon'ble High Court of Himachal Pradesh while considering plethora of cases on the point has concluded that FIR registered for offence under Sections 363, 376, 212, 120-B of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act,
can be quashed on the basis of compromise where prosecutrix has solemnized marriage with accused to enable both the parties to lead life of respect and dignity in the society.

entities.text: Ranjeet Kumar Vs. State of H.P. and Ors. (2023 SCC Online HP 1625)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Once there is no dispute remains between them, then obviously the law cannot be so harsh so as to stand between the parties.

10. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the ratio laid down in aforesaid cases, in the considered opinion of this Court, taking note of the compromise between the parties, the FIR in this case may also be quashed in the interest of justice.

Resultantly, petition stands allowed and FIR bearing Crime No.1028 of 2023 registered at Police Station Cantt., District Guna (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 506 of IPC against the petitioner as well as consequential proceedings stand quashed against petitioner.
Petitioner is set free.
11. Petition stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.
